findings.where: Screen 7, Row times column (text and its read)
findings.what: The screen states that each entry is a row of A times a column of B but never links this to what screens 1 to 3 built, so the reason is skipped in the live lesson, where the explain text is not shown; add one sentence such as "Column 1 of B is where B sends i, and A then works on that point row by row."

findings.where: Screen 5, Both orders (and the lesson as a whole)
findings.what: The identity matrix is never named on any screen, only as a Do nothing button, although the brief promises it as the do-nothing move that acts like 1 and lesson 5's AA⁻¹ = I needs it; add something like "Do nothing is the identity matrix [1 0; 0 1]. Like times 1, it changes nothing, in either order."
This puzzle tests the size rule, but no SHOW screen states it first, so it is learned only from the hint; screen 7 could add "So a row and a column must be the same length."

findings.where: Screens 1 and 3, Two moves, one matrix / Where j ends
findings.what: The screens assert that one matrix makes the whole run but never say why: each move keeps the grid a grid with the origin fixed, so the two together do too; that reason is only in the explain text, which a steps lesson does not show.
"Set each card to a move, then Swap or Play" does not point him to the telling cases where the order stops mattering, which only the read version names; add "Try Turn on both, or Do nothing on one."
"The shear moves nothing on the across axis" reads awkwardly; "The shear leaves every point on the across axis where it is" says it plainly.

findings.where: Screen 8, Work out PQ, hint for [2 4; 0 0]
findings.what: "Run row 1 of P down column 1 of Q and add" mixes the directions; match the practice wording: "Run along row 1 of P and down column 1 of Q, multiply the pairs and add."

findings.where: Screen 11, Mixed: where j ends, hint and slip for (−1, −1)
findings.what: The hint blames reading row 1 of MS, a matrix this screen never shows him, when the likelier slip is flipping both parts; try "M flips only the across part, so the up part stays 1."

The lead is a sentence without a verb describing the grid and flag, but screens 7 to 12 show no grid; try "Each screen shows two matrix cards and their product, most with the F-shaped flag on squared paper."

"The two labels end up facing different ways" is unclear, because both end face down after the flip and the print is hidden; say one ends upside down compared with the other, and make the label clear acetate or say to follow its outline.

"Some pairs of moves give the same result in either order, two turns on the bench" is true of the label too, so it is a caveat, not a place where the analogy breaks; move it to the analogy text or drop it.

The brief's route-counting example is dropped (from a or b through c, d or e to f or g, as a product of two route grids), so the lesson has no use for the product beyond the flag; one SHOW screen or a practice line would restore it.

findings.where: interactive.whatAmILookingAt (printed in the dossier as "What you're looking at")
findings.what: It carries build notes such as "written large enough to read at 360 px", "On a narrow phone these buttons wrap onto more lines without splitting a word" and "Its still is ..., read as:", and it lists every puzzle with its answers and hints, which the dossier says it never prints; cut it to what the picture shows.
